==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|prise}}, from {{der|en|fro|prise||a taking, capture, a seizure, a thing seized, a prize, booty, also hold, purchase}}, past participle of {{m|fro|prendre||to take, to capture}}, from {{der|en|la|prēndō|alt=prēndere||to take, seize}}; see {{m|en|prehend}}. Compare {{m|en|prison}}, {{m|en|apprise}}, {{m|en|comprise}}, {{m|en|enterprise}}, {{m|en|purprise}}, {{m|en|reprisal}}, {{m|en|surprise}}, etc. {{doublet|en|prise}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹaɪ̯z/|a=RP,GA,CA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-prize.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɑ̟ɪ̯z/|/ˈpɹɒ̈ɪ̯z/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹaːz/|a=Southern US,ZA,[[w:Monophthongization|/aɪ̯/-ungliding]]}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪz|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|prize}} * {{homophones|en|pries|prise}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # That which is taken from another; something [[captured]]; a thing seized by force, stratagem, or superior power. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|4|4|page=54|text={{...}} wherefore he now begunne
To challenge her anew, as his owne '''prize''',
Whom formerly he had in battell wonne,}} # {{lb|en|military|nautical}} Anything captured by a [[belligerent]] using the rights of war; especially, property captured at sea in virtue of the rights of war, as a [[vessel]]. #* {{RQ:Johnson History of the Pyrates|chapter=Of Captain [[w:Henry Every|Avery]], and His Crew|page=51|passage=Having taken all the Treasure on Board their own Ships, and plundered their '''Prize''' of every Thing elſe they either wanted or liked, they let her go; ſhe not being able to continue her Voyage, returned back: {{...}}}} # An [[honour]] or [[reward]] striven for in a competitive contest; anything offered to be competed for, or as an [[inducement]] to, or reward of, effort. #: {{ux|en|A literary '''prize''' has been instituted for this [[SY]].}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Aureng-zebe|5|text=I fought and conquer’d, yet have lost the '''prize'''.}} # That which may be won by chance, as in a [[lottery]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1928|author=w:Weston Jarvis|title=Jottings from an Active Life|location=London|publisher=Heath Cranton|page=256|url=https://books.google.ca/books/about/Jottings_from_an_Active_Life.html?id=7J7CtAEACAAJ&redir_esc=y |passage={{w|Cecil Rhodes}} {{...}} was never tired of impressing upon one that the fact of being an Englishman was “the greatest '''prize''' in the lottery of life,” and that it was that thought which always sustained him when he was troubled.}} # Anything worth striving for; a valuable possession held or in [[prospect]]. #* {{RQ:KJV|Philippians|3|14|text=I press toward the mark for the '''prize''' of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[contest]] for a reward; [[competition]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|III|2|text=Like one of two contending in a '''prize''',
That thinks he hath done well in people's eyes {{...}}}} # A [[lever]]; a [[pry]]; also, the hold of a lever. #: {{synonyms|en|prise}} =====Usage notes===== Do not confuse with {{m|en|price}}. {{der|en|enm|prysen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|priser|alt=preisier|t=to set a price or value on, esteem, value}}, from {{m|fro|pris||price}}, from {{der|en|la|pretium||price, value}}, whence Compare {{m|en|appraise}}, {{m|en|apprize}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # To consider highly valuable; to [[esteem]]. #: {{syn|en|honor|regard|respect|Thesaurus:revere}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Tempest|III|1|text={{...}} I
Beyond all limit of what else i’ the world
Do love, '''prize''', honour you.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Aureng-zebe|chapter=V|page=83|text=I '''pris’d''' your Person, but your Crown disdain.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=w:J. M. Coetzee|title=w:The Childhood of Jesus|location=London|publisher=Harvill Secker|chapter=20|page=167|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=NhPDhl0yABIC&printsec=frontcover#v=onepage&q&f=false |passage=‘{{...}} An old broken cup has no value. No one '''prizes''' it.’
‘I '''prize''' it. It’s my museum, not yours.’}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To set or estimate the value of; to appraise; to price; to rate. #: {{syn|en|esteem|evaluate|Thesaurus:appraise}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Winter's Tale|III|2|text={{...}} no life,
I '''prize''' it not a straw, but for mine honour,}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Zechariah|11|13|text={{...}} a goodly price that I was '''prized''' at.}} # To move with a [[lever]]; to force up or open; to [[prise]] or [[pry]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To compete in a [[prizefight]]. =====Derived terms===== {{col4|en|disprize |foreprize |outprize |overprize |prizable |prizer |underprize |unprizable |unprized }} =====Translations===== {{trans-top-see|1. to consider something highly valuable|appreciate}} * Albanian: * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Dutch: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Ido: * Japanese: * Latin: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Swedish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|2. to set or estimate the value of; to appraise|appraise}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Finnish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|3. to move with a lever; to force up or open; to pry|pry}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Dutch: * Finnish: * Japanese: * Māori: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 3=== {{rfe|en}} ====Adjective==== {{en-adj|-}} # Having [[win|won]] a [[#Noun|prize]]; [[award-winning]]. #: {{ux|en|a '''prize''' vegetable}} # {{cap|first-rate}}; [[exceptional]]. #: {{ux|en|He was a '''prize''' fool.}} ===Etymology 4=== Alternative forms. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{obsolete form of|en|price}}. {{defdate|16th–19th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1777|author=w:Joshua Reynolds|editors=w:John Ingamells; w:John Edgcumbe|title=The Letters of Sir Joshua Reynolds|publisher=Yale|year_published=2000|page=69 |passage=My '''prizes''' – for a head is thirty five Guineas – As far as the Knees seventy – and for a whole-length one hundred and fifty.}} ===Further reading=== * {{R:Webster 1913}} * {{R:Century}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=eiprz|pizer|rezip}}
